title: Part Four, Chapter 3: The War of the Peoples

verses.t: And then the peoples consulted again: "What shall we do with these? For truly their power is great when it is used," they said again, when they met in council. "What must be done is to overpower them, defeat them and kill them. We shall arm ourselves with arrows and shields. Are we not many? Not one of them, not any of them, shall be left," they said when they took counsel. And all the peoples armed themselves, and many killers from all the peoples gathered. And Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam were on the top of the mountain called Hacavitz, and there they kept their children safe upon the mountain. And they were few, not like the multitude of the peoples, and the summit of the mountain that they had fortified was small. So it was that the peoples planned that they should be killed, when they all gathered and were summoned.

And this was the gathering of all the peoples, who were all now armed with arrows and shields; and the silver of their adornment could not be counted, and all the lords and soldiers were handsome; and truly they knew how to do what they said: "And all of them shall be captives, and Tohil shall be our god, and we shall greet him and only take him captive," they said among themselves. And Tohil knew all of this, and Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab and Mahucutah knew it too; they heard everything that was planned, because they did not sleep from the time the enemies all armed themselves with arrows and shields. And then all the warriors rose up and planned to attack them by night when they set out; but they did not arrive, for all the soldiers stayed awake on the road. And then they were defeated by Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab and Mahucutah; all of them kept watch together on the road, and without noticing it they all fell asleep. And then their beards and their eyebrows began to be plucked out, and then the silver was stripped from them, from their necks, with the jades, and from their necks and their staffs. And they took the silver only as a lesson and a punishment for them, and it was done to deceive them, as a sign of the greatness of the Quichés. And waking up again, in great haste they felt for their jades and their staffs, and there was no longer any silver on their necks, nor their jades. "Who is this," they said, "who has robbed us? Or who is this who has plucked us? Where did this one come from who has stolen our silver?" said all the soldiers. "Perhaps it is that demon who steals men? Come, we must not be afraid of them for that; we shall take their town, and so we shall get our silver back again. What shall we do to them?" said all the peoples, all those who kept their word. And likewise the chief lords were very calm on the mountain, and Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam knew very well what they were to do. And having taken counsel, Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam made a wall at the edge of the town, setting only small flat stones around the town; and then they made dolls as if they were men, and then they set them in order on the wall, and they had their shields and their arrows; and they put on them their silver jewels and their clothes. And they were only dolls, on whom they put the silver of the peoples which they had gone and stolen on the road; and with this they adorned the dolls, and set them all around the town. And then they went to ask Tohil's counsel: "Will they kill us, or will they defeat us?" And Tohil said to them, "There is no need to worry, for I am here, and this is what you will put against them. Do not be afraid," it was said to Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam.
